experiment.question: With one snmp-config attribute changed, max-repetitions 2 to 5, where does the same 200-thread collector stop completing its cycle at 50 to 100 ms per PDU, and what binds there?
experiment.plan: Hold everything from the pool-200 search (netem delay 75ms 25ms on the simulator, Collectd threads 200) and change one thing: max-repetitions 5 for the 10.42.0.0/16 range, applied through the Config Manager REST API. Verify the change on the wire before measuring. Grow the fleet from 5,250 in steps of 1,000 to 10,000, then 500, one 900 s window per rung, stop at the first rung that fails. Search upward only: nl6 has no selective delete. After the knee at 200 threads, the pool was raised to 300 and the search continued from 12,250 in steps of 500 to the cleanroom bracket, to find where the collector stops being thread-bound.

jvm.flags: JAVA_HEAP_SIZE=10240, JAVA_INITIAL_HEAP_SIZE=8192, -XX:+UseG1GC, -XX:NativeMemoryTracking=summary, MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=4 (systemd drop-in), Prometheus JMX exporter on 9299.

parameters.collectd_threads: 200 for the search; one rung at 300 on the failing fleet

figures.title: Collectd thread pool occupancy across the ten fleet sizes
figures.note: JMX gauge from Collectd itself. Each rung is a 900 s window separated by a provisioning step. The pool fills one rung at a time and is pinned at 200 only in the last.

figures.title: Collectd pending queue, rolling one-minute peak and floor
figures.note: The floor is the pass test. It returns to zero in every rung up to 11,750 and never at 12,250.

figures.title: Collectd task completion ratio and collectable services
figures.note: The ratio is a sawtooth whose median depends on the window's phase and is not part of the pass criterion. Services are divided by 1,000 to share the axis, so 12.25 is 12,254.

figures.title: Collections completed per second against the rate each fleet requires
Samples per second delivered against the rate the fleet requires
figures.note: The completion counter multiplied by the 1,738 samples every fleet collection carries, decoded from the topic. Required is the collectable service count over the 300 s interval, times the same 1,738. A window integral is the honest rate; the rolling rate is shown for shape.

figures.title: Core CPU against the thread pool: the control
figures.note: Node Exporter for CPU, JMX for the pool, on one axis. Unlike the two earlier searches, CPU climbs with the pool: at max-repetitions 5 a thread waits a third as long per collection, so the same pool does three times the work.

figures.title: Core JVM heap and old-generation collections
figures.note: The heap floor climbs with the fleet, from 4.1 GiB at 5,250 to 8.3 GiB at 11,750 under a 10 GiB ceiling, and the first old-generation collections of the whole campaign at this latency appear at 12,250.

figures.title: Minion CPU and the SNMP bridge under injected latency
figures.note: The Minion executes the walks the Core's threads wait on. Its CPU and the SNMP bridge both scale with the fleet; neither is near a limit.

series.label: SNMP on the sim bridge, Mbit/s

figures.title: The 300-thread search: pool occupancy and Core CPU from 12,250 to 14,250
figures.note: Five rungs at 300 threads separated by provisioning steps, two of them two hours long while the driver waited on a node that never scanned. The pool's troughs between waves rise as the CPU climbs past 85%, and in the last rung the pool is pinned because collections take longer, not because there are more of them.

figures.title: The 300-thread search: heap and old-generation collections
figures.note: Old-generation collections go from 15 per window at 12,250 to 36 at 14,250, and the JVM's share of wall time in GC from 11% to 22%. This is the cleanroom's ceiling, reached at the cleanroom's fleet size.

answers.question: With max-repetitions 5 and 200 threads, where does Collectd stop completing its cycle at 50 to 100 ms per PDU?
What did the attribute change on the wire, and how was it applied?
How many metrics does this fleet produce, and at which rung?
What binds at the knee now: the pool, the processor, or the heap?
How far does the pool of 300 carry, and what stops it?
What did the attribute buy against the two earlier searches?

gaps.question: Where exactly between 13,750 and 14,250 is the CPU knee?
gaps.why: The step is 500 and the two rungs straddle the cleanroom's 14,004; the failing rung is not marginal (throughput fell, GC 22% of wall time), so the knee sits in the lower half of the bracket. Locating it finer means 250-device rungs at two hours each under the import race.

gaps.question: Were the two timed-out rungs at steady state?
gaps.why: At 13,750 and 14,250 one node of the 500 added never scanned; the driver waited two hours, then measured with that node at zero interfaces. One collectable service in 14,000 that yields nothing does not move the counters, but the two-hour hold means those fleets had run far longer before their window than the others.

gaps.question: Does 58 requests per collection hold for every device?
gaps.why: It was read for one device over one collection and matches the count derived from the code within 5%; the per-response truncation nl6 documents means devices with long interface names may take one request more.

gaps.question: Is uniform latency the right shape?
gaps.why: netem's default is uniform between the bounds. Real agent response time is heavy-tailed. Under Little's law the same mean should give the same pool occupancy, but that was not tested here.

gaps.question: Do real agents honour max-repetitions 5 as nl6 does?
gaps.why: nl6 truncates to the datagram budget with noError, per its own documentation. A Cisco IOS XR agent at a 1,500-byte packet size should behave the same at 5; that is a documentation reading, not a measurement.

gaps.question: Was each rung at steady state?
gaps.why: Each window opened after the rung's nodes reconciled to nodes x 144 interfaces and provisiond went idle, then a 300 s settle. One window per rung, three cycles, no repetition. OpenNMS was restarted at 11:50Z, ten minutes before the first rung, so the first rung started from an empty queue.

gaps.question: How much of the Core's CPU is collection?
gaps.why: The rolling rescan runs about 40% of the time at the stock provisiond pool and cost about 5 CPU points in the cleanroom; it was not separated out here.
